Repair the remaining audited defects in PR #4 NotificationCenter in place. Preserve the good first repair: production must continue to avoid NotificationCenter-owned UIEdgeInsets, UIVibrancyEffect, and NSExtensionContext; keep the corrected file-scoped UIKit/Foundation imports, the internal/@_spi(OpenUIKitHost) PortableKind surface, the useful enum/controller behavior, and honest fail-closed host behavior.

The residual blocker is false dependency-integration evidence. tests/agent/test_platform_identities.sh currently compiles tests/agent/platform-stage/StagedFoundation.swift as a module named Foundation and StagedUIKit.swift as UIKit. Those files invent NSObject, NSObjectProtocol, NSExtensionContext, CGFloat, CGSize, NSLock, UIEdgeInsets, UIVibrancyEffectStyle, and UIVibrancyEffect. They are test-owned lookalikes, not the real guest platform dependencies requested by the repair, and they cannot prove compatibility with the platform. The current shared platform has real UIKit UIEdgeInsets/UIVibrancyEffect sources but does not yet expose Foundation.NSExtensionContext. Do not paper over that missing dependency by manufacturing a module named Foundation.

Rework the gates so any integration-labelled probe consumes actual staged platform Foundation and UIKit module/dylib outputs from this repository. The client must explicitly accept UIKit.UIEdgeInsets and UIKit.UIVibrancyEffect and must assign the context as Foundation.NSExtensionContext. It must inspect the NotificationCenter interface/symbols for the absence of NotificationCenter-owned nominals and link/load libNotificationCenter.dylib. If actual Foundation.NSExtensionContext is unavailable, report that exact central dependency blocker instead of substituting a fixture and do not emit a platform-success marker. A synthetic unit fixture may remain only behind an explicit test-only mode, with an unmistakable unit-fixture/standalone-only marker, and must never be cited as platform identity evidence.

Audit coverage honestly. In particular, the three NSExtensionContext rows, four UIVibrancyEffect rows, and NCWidgetProviding.widgetMarginInsets row cannot remain implemented solely because the synthetic staging test passes. Mark them declared/deferred as appropriate until a real dependency build compiles and exercises them; retain implemented status for independently exercised behavior. Preserve every one of the 28 exact coverage IDs and the lane floor.

Repair the remaining audited defects in PR #8 CoreServices in place. Preserve the good first repair: retain all 150 coverage IDs; keep the honest 24 runtime-asserted constants and 115 compile-only constants unless stronger evidence is added; keep CoreServices as owner of the iPhone UTI surface and MobileCoreServices as adapter/reexport; preserve the exact dyn.* oracle question and current nil fail-closed partial; retain the documented duplicate registries/constants/five divergent records; and keep the explicit statement and guard that this Swift overlay does not emit or claim `_UTType*`/`_kUT*` C ABI exports. The C ABI deferral is correct and must not be regressed.

The residual blocker is Swift source-signature drift. The immutable public surface requires CFString parameters and these exact ownership-bearing returns: UTTypeCopyPreferredTagWithClass -> Unmanaged<CFString>?, UTTypeCopyAllTagsWithClass -> Unmanaged<CFArray>?, UTTypeCopyDeclaration -> Unmanaged<CFDictionary>?, UTTypeCopyDeclaringBundleURL -> Unmanaged<CFURL>?, UTTypeCopyDescription -> Unmanaged<CFString>?, UTTypeCreatePreferredIdentifierForTag -> Unmanaged<CFString>?, and UTTypeCreateAllIdentifiersForTag -> Unmanaged<CFArray>?. Current production replaces them with String/[String]/[String: Any]/URL and direct optionals. Existing callers that invoke takeRetainedValue() therefore do not compile, so README's Swift source-compatibility claim is false. CoreServicesIdentityProbe.swift merely asserts the weakened signatures and cannot validate the pinned API.

Use the actual staged platform Foundation/CoreFoundation identities and make the public signatures match the immutable declarations, including Unmanaged ownership and CFArray. Update the identity probe to assign every public function to closures with the exact pinned CF/Unmanaged types, pass real values across CoreFoundation/CoreServices, and reject direct-optional substitutes. Do not create CoreServices-local CF aliases or a test-owned CoreFoundation lookalike. The current shared CoreFoundationCompatibility aliases CFString to String and lacks an ownership-capable CFArray; if that prevents exact Unmanaged signatures, treat it as a central dependency blocker. In that case move any portable direct-value helpers out of the canonical public surface to internal/@_spi(OpenUIKitHost), mark the seven ownership-return rows deferred rather than implemented, and stop claiming full Swift source compatibility. Do not weaken the immutable interface merely to make a fixture compile.

Keep coverage honest and above the 120 implemented|declared lane floor. The seven wrong-signature functions cannot remain implemented as canonical rows until the exact public declarations compile; independently tested registry behavior may remain implemented through internal/SPI helpers. Preserve the correct 35/115 behavior accounting where still valid, adjusting only rows affected by exact signature availability. Continue auditing the produced Swift symbols for the absence of claimed C exports; absence is not implementation of the C ABI.

Repair the remaining audited defects in PR #9 Social in place. Preserve every good first-repair change: keep the correct file-scoped UIKit/Accounts/FoundationNetworking imports; UITextViewDelegate conformance and delegate wiring; cancel -> didSelectCancel without recursion; honestly partial didSelectPost/didSelectCancel host semantics; completionHandler clearing; at most one pushed configuration controller; account-nonnull preparedURLRequest failure without OAuth; non-networking perform; init! alignment and documented unavoidable stronger override; @_spi(OpenUIKitHost) non-Apple helpers; five service constants declared; and the current honest dependency-bound coverage downgrades.

First residual: production fallback selection is still implicit. SocialHostTypes.swift publishes Social.UIView, UIViewController, UIImage, UITextView, and UITextViewDelegate in the ordinary `#else` whenever UIKit is absent. SLRequest.swift similarly publishes Social.ACAccount whenever UIKit and Accounts are absent. Replace this with one explicit isolated-test compilation flag such as SOCIAL_STANDALONE_TEST_FIXTURES. Only that flag may enable fallback declarations, and the resulting dylib/markers must say standalone-unit-fixture-only. In every ordinary production configuration, missing UIKit or Accounts must fail compilation with a clear dependency blocker; Social must never silently acquire those nominal identities.

Second residual: tests/agent/test_platform_identity.sh manufactures OpenUIKit, UIKit, and Accounts from tests/agent/staging and labels the result platform identity. Those are useful only as explicit unit fixtures. A real integration gate must consume actual staged platform Foundation, UIKit/OpenUIKit implementation, and Accounts outputs from the repository, never compile replacement dependency APIs inside full/social/tests. Its compile client should accept dependency values without assuming a fake zero-argument ACAccount initializer, prove the exact UIKit superclass/protocol/image/text-view/controller types and Accounts.ACAccount property type, inspect the Social interface/symbol graph for no Social-owned dependency types, link/load libSocial.dylib, and emit a marker unique to real integration. Accounts is not currently staged in the shared platform; if still missing, report that exact blocker and retain the affected rows as declared/deferred. Do not use a lookalike to turn the blocker green.

Third residual: complete multipart hardening. addMultipartData validates name/type/filename, but when multipart is active parameter dictionary keys become URLQueryItem names and are inserted verbatim into `Content-Disposition: form-data; name=...`; reject or safely encode CR, LF, and quote contamination for every multipart field name, including parameter-derived fields. Add focused injection tests. multipartBoundary checks only 16 candidates and then returns an unchecked final UUID candidate. Every returned boundary must have been collision-tested against all parameter names/values and part metadata/data. Refactor an internal/SPI candidate source if needed so a deterministic test can force collisions and prove retry behavior; never return an unchecked fallback.

Reconcile all 67 coverage rows after these changes, preserving every exact ID and the lane floor. Keep real local behavior implemented, dependency identity compile-only rows declared, and unavailable host-service behavior honest. A fixture-only runtime cannot prove UIKit/Accounts integration or Apple host behavior.
